320x50.notes: Must be submitted at 640x100 (2x). 50 KB static maximum.

970x250.notes: 1940x500 required onsite in North America. Amazon's custom below-the-fold billboard spec is stricter: max 20 words, max three typography variations, headline and body no smaller than 36 points.

414x125.notes: Amazon mobile shopping format. Supply at 828x250 with a 640x250 safe zone. Amazon may supply the CTA separately, so the safe zone prioritises product, brand and headline. (CTA baked in per Smart 1 request; Amazon may also overlay its own.)

300x250.notes: Desktop. 40 KB static maximum — Amazon's published rule is 40 KB for every static desktop unit except the billboard, which takes 200 KB. That is the US ceiling; FR, IT, ES and JP allow 50 KB, and building to the lower one is what makes a single file deliverable in every market Smart 1 buys.
300x250._verifiedAgainst: Amazon DSP desktop static display specs, re-checked 2026-08-30: the 40 KB rule for all non-billboard static desktop units is what covers this size. Previously carried as an assumption by analogy with 728x90 and 160x600, which the rule confirms.

250x250._verifiedAgainst: NOT CONFIRMED. Every other size here was read off Amazon's desktop static spec sheet; this one never was, and two independent readings of Amazon's published DSP static list on 2026-08-30 enumerate 300x250, 728x90, 160x600, 300x600, 970x250, 320x50 and 414x125 and do not include 250x250 at all. So both halves are open: whether Amazon traffics this unit, and whether 50 KB is its ceiling when the published rule for standard desktop static units is 40 KB. Left exactly as it was rather than guessed at in either direction -- raising the ceiling ships a file Amazon may refuse, and lowering it steps the quality ladder down to satisfy a limit that may not exist, which is the mistake meta.json made with Google's 150 KB. Confirm against Amazon's own spec sheet before the next Amazon delivery.
